headline: Sox Offense Puts Us To Sleep In A Brutal Six To One Loss To Toronto
morning_brew: We're right back in the mud after a brutal six to one loss to the Blue Jays at Fenway last night. Payton Tolle gave us five innings on the mound, but he took the loss after giving up three earned runs. The offense just couldn't pick him up, scratching out only one run despite finishing the night with eight hits. I watched that ninth inning through my fingers as Toronto tacked on two more runs to put this one completely out of reach.

That offense was so quiet last night at Fenway that Uncle Carmine actually stayed awake for all nine innings. Carmine lives in Revere and usually dozes off by the third, but even he was too stunned by our lack of run support to sleep. Ceddanne Rafaela had a decent night with two hits, but we didn't string anything together. You're not going to win many ballgames in this league when you can only muster a single run.

Down in Foxborough, Robert Kraft and the Pats are suing the town over nearly one million dollars in security-related license fees. Are you kiddin' me with this? We're trying to build on that Super Bowl appearance from last season, and instead we're reading about lawsuits over Gillette Stadium entertainment licenses. Let the lawyers handle the paperwork so we can focus on getting Drake Maye and this defense ready for training camp.

news_digest.dans_take: Fighting over a million bucks is a bad look when we've got a championship to chase.

news_digest.dans_take: Offseason talk is already getting silly, but I'd take him in a heartbeat.

trend_watch.dans_take: Struck out six batters, but he needs to limit the damage when our bats are this quiet.

trend_watch.dans_take: Two hits on a night where the rest of the lineup went cold shows the kid is trying to spark something.

trend_watch.trend: Surrendered two runs over two innings of relief work
trend_watch.dans_take: Gave up two runs to close out the game, making a tough night look even worse.
